name: Non-Verbal Series
shortcutSummary: Observe how elements change from one figure to the next: rotation (clockwise/anticlockwise), addition/removal of elements, movement of elements, and change in shading. Apply the pattern to predict the next figure.
conceptExplanation:
Non-Verbal Series questions show a sequence of figures that change according to a pattern. You must identify the pattern and select the next figure in the series.

Common patterns: rotation, element addition/subtraction, size change, shading alternation, and position shifting.

subtopics.name: Non-Verbal Series — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation:
Non-Verbal Series questions show a sequence of figures that change according to a pattern. You must identify the pattern and select the next figure in the series.

Common patterns: rotation, element addition/subtraction, size change, shading alternation, and position shifting.
shortcuts: Rotation Tracking: Note if elements rotate clockwise or anticlockwise and by how many degrees per step.
Element Count: Check if elements increase or decrease by a fixed number each step.
Multiple Pattern Overlay: Often, different elements in the same figure follow different independent patterns.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Identify the next figure in the given sequential series:

An arrow pointing North in Fig 1, North-East in Fig 2, East in Fig 3, South-East in Fig 4.
options: An arrow pointing South-West (rotated 225°)
An arrow pointing West (rotated 270°)
An arrow pointing directly South (45° clockwise rotation)
An arrow pointing North-West (rotated 315°)
practiceQuestions.hint: Track the angle of rotation, side addition, or position shifting of key elements from frame to frame.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The arrow rotates systematically clockwise by 45° in each successive step: 0° (N) -> 45° (NE) -> 90° (E) -> 135° (SE) -> 180° (S).
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Identify the dynamic element changing across frames.
Step 2: Determine the mathematical step rule (e.g. +45° rotation or +1 line segment).
Step 3: Apply the rule to the 4th figure to predict: An arrow pointing directly South (45° clockwise rotation).
